chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-salam (advance payment for goods) in foodstuff, with a known measure, until a known term. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.إِلَى أَجَلٍ مَعْلُومٍ: Until a known term/time, specifying the delivery deadline.
key_terms.السَّلَم: A specific type of sale where payment is made in advance for goods to be delivered later at a fixed date.
key_terms.الطَّعَام: Foodstuff, the commodity subject to the contract.
key_terms.بِكَيْلٍ مَعْلُومٍ: With a known measure/quantity, a condition for validity.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible.

ai.seo_question: Is advance payment for future delivery of food permissible in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the contract of *al-salam* (advance payment for goods), a practice crucial for agricultural financing in early Islamic society. The Imam’s affirmation underscores the necessity of precise specification (*kayl ma'lum*) and a fixed deadline (*ajal ma'lum*) to prevent the *gharar* (uncertainty) that would otherwise invalidate the trade. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical economic facilitation while maintaining strict contractual clarity.
